look_here_first: Start at the flowering stalk: S. eulae typically has GLABROUS peduncles, nearly horizontal to spreading branches and conspicuously serrate roughish leaves. Count rays on an intact head, commonly 27–36, and check the hemispheric involucre usually 5–6.5 mm. S. drummondii var. texanum has very hairy distal stems and winged lower leaf petioles.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Current Kew accepts S. eulae as Texas-endemic. County occurrence data derived from TORCH herbarium aggregation includes Bexar, Travis, and San Saba.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Exact county evidence; accepted local infraspecific concepts reconciled internally.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Glabrous peduncles, 27–36 rays, 5–6.5 mm hemispheric head; versus Texas drummondii with hairy distal shoots and winged-petiolate lower leaves.
